- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at +3-4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed, model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1-2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5-1.0 point upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average of sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model misreads momentum; apply 10-20% dampening to forecast slope.
